thread:
Tara Nguyen: heads up — getting a few support tickets where billing shows org A but auth logs attribute requests to a service account. Can we root cause?
Ben Ortiz: saw two of those. proxy fallback is weird: when X-Origin missing, it grabs SA mapping and marks request as `sa` origin.
Mike Chen: confirming — current heuristic is: project claim > X-Origin header > SA-map lookup. Legacy keys often lack project claim/header so end up as SA.
Tara Nguyen: that's the issue — legacy (projectless) keys should be attributed to the org owner, not an arbitrary SA mapping. It's polluting SA quotas/dashboards.
Joan Patel: UX impact is rough — customers see quota spikes on SAs they don't own. :confused:
Ben Ortiz: repro steps quick: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <legacy-key>\" https://api.redwood.test/v1/engines` -> 200, proxy sets `X-Resolved-Origin: sa:svc-42` in logs.
Mike Chen: payload snippet from proxy resolver for context:
```
input: {claims: null, headers: {authorization}, sa_map_lookup: svc-42}
resolved_origin: \"sa:svc-42\"
```
Ben Ortiz: we never tag how we decided, so console can't show \"this was inferred via SA map\" vs asserted by token.
Liam O'Connor: options: 1) change heuristic to prefer org-owner for legacy keys; 2) add explicit provenance tag so console can show inference method; 3) backfill telemetry and adjust dashboards.
Tara Nguyen: prefer low-risk path first: add provenance tag + metric so we can observe impact, then decide if heuristic change is needed.
Joan Patel: for UX, show two columns in auth events table: `origin` and `origin_provenance` with tooltip explaining values. e.g. `inferred:sa-map`, `asserted:claim`, `header`.
Mike Chen: implementation sketch: auth service returns JSON header `X-Auth-Provenance: claim|header|sa-map|legacy-default` and also includes `X-Resolved-Origin` as today. Update gateway to preserve both.
Ben Ortiz: metric plan: emit `auth.provenance` tag on auth events and add a counter `auth.origin_inferred_total{method=...}`. Also histogram `auth.origin_latency_ms`.
Tara Nguyen: rollout plan: dev -> staging -> 10% prod (canary) -> gradual. We'll monitor `auth.origin_inferred_total{method=sa-map}` and affected customer list.
Liam O'Connor: telemetry backfill: we can run a query over logs for last 30 days to estimate who will flip quotas. Put those accounts in a warning queue.
Joan Patel: UX message: add inline notice in console quotas page for affected SAs: "This SA attribution may be inferred for legacy keys — contact support to reassign."
Mike Chen: PR checklist: schema bump for auth headers, gateway pass-through tests, unit tests for resolver order, integration test that checks header preservation.
Ben Ortiz: I'll draft customer-facing note once we have numbers. Suggest tagging top 50 accounts and PM review.
Tara Nguyen: one more: should billing pipeline treat `inferred` origin as provisional for 48 hours before committing to charge buckets? Otherwise customers will see immediate billing shifts.
Liam O'Connor: good call. Add `provisional=true` flag to billing event if provenance != asserted. We'll need a cleanup job to reconcile after 48h.
Mike Chen: also ensure reconciliation is idempotent and emits audit events.
Tara Nguyen: great. Ben, Mike — please open PRs and link the staging dashboard. We'll sync tomorrow after staging metrics. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: auth-provenance v1 -> staging (build #2026).
Joan Patel: any objections to the provisional approach?
Mike Chen: none from infra; need to ensure reconciliation job is idempotent.
Ben Ortiz: tagging owners on the PRs now.
